body:
_This PR has been manually self reviewed_

Video overview to help with the review: https://youtu.be/-JhKcZttXp8

# Objective

Fix a regression where string DevContainer lifecycle commands lost their argument boundaries. For example, a `postCreateCommand` of `npm update` executed only `npm`, causing the remaining arguments to be silently ignored.

Fixes: #62964 

## Solution

Pass lifecycle commands to Docker as distinct command arguments instead of flattening them into a space-separated string. This preserves the command exactly as configured and prevents Docker from reinterpreting it as separate arguments.

This PR also fixes `postStartCommand` handling, which this PR would have caused to stop working (it depended on the previous behavior). Its marker handling now matches the [upstream Dev Container CLI](https://github.com/devcontainers/cli/blob/33073dbaba2545c51b4f8396e179c18231e80124/src/spec-common/injectHeadless.ts#L2854-L2867).

## Testing

Create a directory called `zed-lifecycle-test`  to be open as a project with a devcontainer.

Add the file `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` to that folder with these contents:

```json
{
    "name": "zed-lifecycle-test",
    "image": "mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:ubuntu",

    // Fixes the hostname so shell prompts and logs identify the container.
    "runArgs": ["--hostname", "zed-lifecycle-test"],

    "initializeCommand": ".devcontainer/lifecycle.sh initializeCommand",
    "onCreateCommand": ".devcontainer/lifecycle.sh onCreateCommand",
    "updateContentCommand": ".devcontainer/lifecycle.sh updateContentCommand",
    "postCreateCommand": ".devcontainer/lifecycle.sh postCreateCommand",
    "postStartCommand": ".devcontainer/lifecycle.sh postStartCommand",
    "postAttachCommand": ".devcontainer/lifecycle.sh postAttachCommand"
}
```

also add a file `.devcontainer/lifecycle.sh` with these contents:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

echo "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) ${1} ran (pid $$)" | tee -a lifecycle.log
```

You can get these files here: https://github.com/pupeno/zed-workspace/tree/main/lifecycle

Open it with regular Zed and you'll see a dialog with the error:

> Failed to start Dev Container. See logs for details
> DevContainer creation failed
> [OK]

The log will show:

```
2026-08-27T19:43:33+01:00 ERROR [recent_projects::remote_servers] Failed to start dev container: DevContainerUpFailed("Failed with nested error: DevContainerScriptsFailed")
```

Run Zed (`cargo run`) from this branch, open the directory `zed-lifecycle-test` and then either accept the offer to open it as a devcontainer or trigger it yourself. It should created a `zed-lifecycle-test/lifecycle.log` that contains:

```
2026-08-27T18:42:38Z initializeCommand ran (pid 514191)
2026-08-27T18:42:40Z onCreateCommand ran (pid 14)
2026-08-27T18:42:40Z updateContentCommand ran (pid 24)
2026-08-27T18:42:41Z postCreateCommand ran (pid 34)
2026-08-27T18:42:41Z postStartCommand ran (pid 53)
2026-08-27T18:42:41Z postAttachCommand ran (pid 63)
```

Run relevant tests with:

```
cargo test -p dev_container
```

## Self-Review Checklist:

- [x] I've reviewed my own diff for quality, security, and reliability
- [x] Unsafe blocks (if any) have justifying comments
- [x] The content adheres to Zed's UI standards ([UX/UI](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#uiux-checklist) and [icon](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/blob/main/crates/icons/README.md) guidelines)
- [x] Tests cover the new/changed behavior
- [x] Performance impact has been considered and is acceptable

---

Release Notes:

- Dev Container lifecycle commands with arguments, such as `postCreateCommand: "npm update"`, now run properly.
- Dev Container `postStartCommand` handling now matches upstream.

Hit this on Zed 1.20.2 (macOS, Docker Desktop, arm64) with a Rails project. This PR fixes the issue.

Adding a data point since the symptom is easy to misread.

`devcontainer.json`:

    "postCreateCommand": "npm ci && bundle install"

Zed log:

    ERROR [dev_container::docker] Command produced a non-successful output. StdErr:
    ERROR [recent_projects::remote_servers] Failed to start dev container: DevContainerUpFailed("Failed with nested error: DevContainerScriptsFailed")

Stderr is empty because what runs is `sh -c "/bin/sh -c npm ci && bundle install"`: the inner shell executes bare `npm`, which prints usage to stdout and exits 1. Running the same command by hand with `docker exec` succeeds, so nothing points at the editor.

The same project previously had `yarn install && ...` as the first command. That degraded to bare `yarn`, which means install, so it appeared to work and hid the bug.

Workaround until this merges: only the first command in the string loses its arguments, so a no-op prefix is enough:

    "postCreateCommand": "true && npm ci && bundle install"
